Things to attack specifically (not exhaustive):
  1. Determinism: any host-time or host-order leak into guest-visible timerfd values; wait loops that could
     spin or livelock (claimed: each cap strictly later); clock observations added to programs that watch no timerfd.
  2. Linux fidelity vs fs/timerfd.c: settime validation order (EFAULT, EINVAL flags/timespec, EBADF/EINVAL fd),
     invalid request leaves state unchanged, CANCEL_ON_SET only for REALTIME+ABSTIME, read EINVAL/EAGAIN/ERESTARTSYS,
     gettime, epoll ET/ONESHOT/maxevents semantics, select count and remaining timeout, poll merge.
  3. The four known rescue findings claimed fixed: realtime ABSTIME (no bogus conversion), select count,
     invalid timespec, lifecycle cleanup (OFD-keyed; release, exit, failed exec). Verify each in code AND test.
  4. Mode gate: record/replay and non-sequentialized runs must be byte-for-byte the old host-passthrough behaviour
     (including timerfd_create clock validation by the kernel).
  5. Scheduler: TimedEvent::TimerFdExpiry pop order, removal on disarm/release/exit, stale entries, fast-forward
     when all threads wait on a timerfd, no deadlock report regressions.
  6. Validation bookkeeping (commit d10491308d): the ratchet numbers (856->858, 852->854, 748->760, NON_CI 173->172)
     must equal measured populations; confirm no selector/command/comparator/timeout was relaxed and the expected-plan
     delta is exactly the two cells.
  7. Required markers present: `// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED` at new dispatch entries and
